summary: Lake Murray Airport (LMY) is a small airfield serving the remote Lake Murray region in Papua New Guinea's Western Province, one of the country's most isolated inhabited areas. The airport provides a vital air link for the local communities and supports access to the vast tropical lowland rainforest and the large freshwater lake system that defines the region. It primarily handles light aircraft and charter services due to its short runway and remote location.
faqs:
Q: Where is Lake Murray Airport located?
A: It is situated in the Western Province of Papua New Guinea, near the shores of Lake Murray, one of the largest freshwater lakes in the country.

Q: What type of aircraft use Lake Murray Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves small propeller aircraft and charter flights, as the short runway and remote location are unsuitable for larger commercial jets.

Q: Are there scheduled commercial flights to Lake Murray Airport?
A: Scheduled services are very limited; most flights are chartered or operated on an as-needed basis to serve the surrounding communities and tourism.

Q: What is the main purpose of the airport?
A: It provides essential access for residents, supplies, and visitors to an otherwise roadless region surrounded by dense rainforest and swampland.
transport_tips: There are no roads connecting Lake Murray to major towns, so the airport is effectively the only reliable way in or out of the region. Charter flights from Port Moresby or other provincial centers are the standard means of access, and visitors should arrange transport in advance. The small terminal offers minimal facilities, so plan to arrive prepared with essentials for the journey onward by boat or light vehicle.
local_tip: Book your outbound flight early in the day when possible, as afternoon weather over the surrounding wetlands and forest can cause sudden delays or cancellations common in this part of PNG.
